title: App Store preview
summary: An App Store app preview or Google Play preview video of a mobile app: 15-30 s of the app's own screens at the store's exact size, built to pass review and read muted.

notFor.when: a launch film, ad or promo for social feeds, a site or ads, with no store rules to meet
the film teaches how to do a task in the app step by step

qa: Every frame is a screen capture of the app or a copy overlay on it: no people, hands, fingers, device frame or footage from outside the app (App Store cut)
store:conform returns ok for each store file: the class's exact size, 30 fps or less, 15.0-30.0 s, one stereo AAC track (silent if the film has no sound)
The frame at 5 s is a composed still that states the reason to install; nothing transitions across it
No price, date, seasonal word, ranking or award claim, 'new' or 'best'; purchases or sign-in needed for what is shown are disclosed in the footage or the end frame
The copy alone tells the story with the sound off, and each line holds long enough to read at phone size
Captured UI shows seeded, fictional accounts in the preview's language; content suits a 4+ rating

intake.ask: Which stores and device classes: iPhone, iPad, Mac or Apple TV on the App Store, and/or Google Play?
intake.why: Each class is its own canvas (886x1920, 1200x1600, 1920x1080) and its own capture and render.
intake.default: App Store iPhone 886x1920 portrait and Google Play 1080x1920 portrait

intake.ask: How do we get real footage of the app: a build I can run in the Simulator or on a device, a web build from the repo, or recordings you make on your phone?
intake.why: Apple accepts only screen captures of the app itself; there is no drawn fallback.

intake.ask: Does anything shown need a sign-in, a subscription or an in-app purchase?
intake.why: App Review 2.3.2 requires disclosing it in the footage or the end frame.

intake.ask: What is the one reason to install, and which three to five app moments prove it?
intake.why: It must read by the 5 s poster frame and with the sound off.
intake.default: The feature the store description leads with

intake.ask: Which languages, and how many previews per language (up to three)?
intake.why: Each locale needs the UI re-captured in that language; a missing one falls back to another language.
intake.default: One preview in the app's primary store language

intake.ask: Sound: music and in-app sounds only, or a narrated voice?
intake.why: Previews autoplay muted; a voice is optional, paid and needs every territory licensed.
intake.default: Licensed music and synth UI sounds, no voice

profiles.note: Exact sizes per class: iPhone 886x1920 (1080x1920 only for 5.5"), iPad 1200x1600, Mac/TV 1920x1080; 30 fps max, stereo 256 kbps AAC, muted autoplay, poster frame 5 s.
One public or unlisted YouTube video, ads off, no side bars; real app in the first 10 s; only the first 30 s autoplay, muted; 1024x500 feature graphic required.

starter.note: The capture itself is the picture: ui-camera-read for the rare gentle read of a small control, ui-touch-hotspot for a soft dot at each touch (never a finger), scene-end-card for the app name and the purchase disclosure.

variants.title: Game preview
variants.changes: Gameplay captured on device carries the film, more gameplay than cutscenes (Apple), landscape canvases when the game is landscape (1920x886), in-game sound effects instead of synth UI sounds, no tap hotspots over action.

variants.title: iPad preview
variants.changes: Separate capture and composition at 1200x1600 (or 1600x1200), copy sized for the larger screen; store:conform --class ipad checks it (delivery cannot).
